question: Kosal, Anga, Kashi and Vajji were all:

options.text: ruled by King Harshvardhan in 6th century AD

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kosal, Anga, Kashi, and Vajji** were all part of the **16 Mahajanapadas**.
 
• The **16 Mahajanapadas** were a group of sixteen powerful and vast kingdoms that existed in ancient India.
 
• These Mahajanapadas played a significant role in the political and cultural landscape of ancient India.
 
• The concept of Mahajanapadas is an important aspect of ancient Indian history and is often studied to understand the political and social structures of that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **16 Mahajanapadas** included kingdoms like **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti**, and others.
 
• The term **Mahajanapada** means "great realm" or "great country".
 
• The period of the Mahajanapadas is crucial for understanding the development of political organization in ancient India.
 
• Most of these Mahajanapadas were located in the fertile Indo-Gangetic plains.
 
• This period saw the rise of urban centers and the growth of trade and commerce.
 
• The political structure of these Mahajanapadas varied, with some being monarchies and others being republics.
